I will repeat the three separate texts that I have just read:

1. Narration of a haunted experience:
"I can recall the day when I visited a church that was said to be haunted. The congregation inside seemed to be in a state of constant fear, frequently looking upwards as if expecting something to happen. Despite my own apprehension, I decided to move towards the altar. As I passed the parishioners, they would make the sign of the cross and nervously warn me, 'Don't do that!' Ignoring their remarks, I opened the gate in the rails and stood in front of the altar. Behind it, instead of a reredos, there was a dark red tapestry with a peculiar, curling design, reaching all the way to the roof."

2. Speech about the resurgence of fascism:
"I recount that history because once again we face similar challenges in efforts to confront the rising threat of a new type of fascism. Today, another enemy, a different kind of enemy, has made clear its intentions with attacks in places like New York and Washington, D.C., Bali, London, Madrid, Moscow, and so many other places. But some seem not to have learned history's lessons. With the growing lethality and the increasing availability of weapons, can we truly afford to believe that somehow, some way, vicious extremists can be appeased? Can folks really continue to think that free societies can negotiate with terror?"

3. Personal experience with beauty:
"I want to share an experience that left a deep impression on me. I was once in a place, and after floating around the building, I descended and landed back where I started. As I walked away, someone like Barbara came running towards me in a white coat, shouting, 'Quick, don't let him get out!' But I walked straight into a wood without hesitation. At that moment, I was filled with an overwhelming sense of joy and beauty, which made all my worries disappear. I was standing there, repeating again and again, 'My God, what is that?' And, as always happened in the most significant, singular moments of my life, I received this impression that all this I've experienced was a revelation of sorts."
